steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). In a small bowl, combine cornmeal and milk; let stand for 5 minutes. Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt and sugar. Mix in the cornmeal mixture, eggs and oil until smooth. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until a knife inserted into the center of the cornbread comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Homesteader Cornbread
raw_recipe.description: This moist cornbread with a crisp, golden crust is great with chili or as a quick side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Homesteader Cornbread

review.reviewBody: If your bread is too dense try beating the batter longer next time. In the original recipe It stated to beat for 5 min. I know this seems extreme, but it will help. This helps whip more air into it. When Allrecipes listed this recipe they modified it. Patricia Bergstrom

5/2017: I made this cornbread recipe for the first time today. I used buttermilk since that is what I had on hand and I use it more often for baking. I also made muffins, and reduced the baking time to 15 minutes. The muffins were soft and moist. Very tender! Wonderful with butter and honey. I think soaking the cornmeal in the milk really helped with the final texture. It has taken me many years to find a decent cornbread recipe that is moist...this is it! Will definitely be making this recipe again in the future!
6-24-19 UPDATE: Today I made this recipe using my corn-stick pan. They turned out WONDERFUL!! Crispy on the corn imprint side, soft and tender on the inside. Best & most versatile cornbread recipe ever! When I make the batter I whisk it for at least 5 or 6 minutes to make sure it is smooth with no lumps. I also preheat the cast iron pan that's being used and pour the batter into the hot, oiled pan. Perfect every time! :)
I’ve made at least 5 other cornbread recipes. This one is the BEST I’ve ever made. I used about 3/4 cup of sugar and cooked it in a buttered cast iron Skillet.

excellent cornbread recipe. I used a 9 inch round pan and it was quite tall, and moist. while soaking the corn meal, I stirred it a lot to help it absorb the milk. I also 2as trying to kill time, so I beat my eggs with a whisk until they were quite fluffy, and added the oil to that, mayonnaise-style, until I had a really nice egg/oil emulsion with lots of air trapped,and then added that to the everything else. I didn't the beat the finished mixture for a long time, just enough to get everything mixed, and it turned out beautifully. I used slightly less sugar than called for, otherwise followed the recipe, and got a nice strong corn flavour. this was probably the best cornbread I've ever made. it's really big, though! I had guests so that worked, but be warned! it makes a lot of cornbread!

This is hands down the best corn bread I've ever tasted! I've been hesitant in the past few years to make corn bread because I always find it so dry and crumbly. This was incredibly moist and so delicious! I checked the comments first and made a few changed to the original recipes. 
1-I used even amounts of cornmeal and flour (1 3/4 cups each)
2-I used 1/4 melted butter and 1/4 vegetable oil.
3-I added maybe 1/4 cup of creamed corn (I was using it in another recipe anyways so thought I'd throw some in here)
4-I beat it for 5 minutes on medium high. This was an important step and you could actually see the batter getting larger in the bowl!
5-while I was beating, I put my 12" cast iron pan in the oven with about 2-3 tbsp of butter. 
I made this 3 days ago to go with some chilli. It's STILL moist and so delicious! I will definitely be making this again!!

This was my 1st time making it, and I took the advice of two people on here.
I halved the recipe so I didn't waste a bunch of ingredients if I did mess up. Did equal parts of cornmeal - flour ratio, substituted the milk for buttermilk, kept whisking every so often the cornmeal and buttermilk. I actually kept it longer than 5 mins together cause I was a mess! But that might've helped moistened the cornmeal better. Sifted flour, baking powder, salt, sugar (1/4 c white sugar) and whisked that. Then added the cornmeal mix, egg, 1/2 c melted butter, and 1/2 drained canned corn. I wasn't sure I did something wrong since my batter was not near runny, I added a bit of vegetable oil, but I think it would've been fine without. With that being said, there was in no way could I use a whisk, so I just used a wooden spatula/spoon to just mix it up. Stuck to the 5 mins mix by hand. Used a glass pyrex loaf, and set the oven at °325. It took a longer than 30 mins, not sure how long I left it in for, but went with the clean fork method and took it out to cool. For my 1st time, it was perfect. Some minor mistakes I could correct myself on, but this is the kind I love and I'm sticking to it.

WOW! Best cornbread I've ever had. My hubby loved it so much I'm making another batch today, just finished the first one yesterday. I soaked the corn meal in milk for 10 minutes, beat the batter for 5 and added a small can of corn. I used a Pyrex pan and lowered the temperature to 375. It came out perfectly at 30 minutes. No crumbling! Wonderful! Will make often.

This cornbread turned out great - I did a dairy free version and used one can of coconut milk and topped off with almond milk to get the 2-1/2 cups. I also tried the hint where I mixed the milk and corn meal and let it set for about 20 minutes. Came out super light and fluffy and didn’t fall apart too badly. A keeper!

Very easy, clear recipe and came out as presented. It is forgiving of improvisation. I used butter milk instead of milk and mixed in corn kernels from 3 ears. I reduced the sugar 1/3 by preference. I froze half and eating on the other half

This is the only recipe I use for my blackberry jam cornbread muffins. Just drop a tsp. of cold blackberry jam in center of the muffin before cooking. This is my kids fave and has become a loved childhood memory for them now as adults. I placed this recipe in my own cookbook I’ve written for them.

This has become my “go to” when I need cornbread for another recipe. My daughter cannot tolerate cow milk so I have modified it to be dairy free. Still comes out great. I use Ripple brand 1/2 and 1/2 for 2 cups of the milk and regular Ripple milk for the other half. I also do the modification of 1/3 cup white and 1/3 cup brown sugar. Easy enough to substitute things and make it your own.
Wow better than what I thought it be. Not very sweet, not dry, not overly moist. Nice n fluffy. It's real good.

Very lightly sweet cornbread, good fit for most dishes you'll be serving. Changes I did: for the milk, used 1/2 almond milk and 1/2 half 'n half; for the oil, melted 2T butter and the rest avocado oil. Although I whisked the batter for over 5 minutes, it was ended up pretty dense and didn't rise as well as I'd hoped. That may have made the cornbread a little too chewy. The air bubbles in the batter rose to the top to create a strange, pockmarked surface, which looked even worse after I used the broiler function to brown the top. I'd like to try it again but tweak it to make it lighter and have more corn flavor.
I have been looking for a sheet pan corn bread and using masa. Great find. I used half bacon grease and half coconut oil.

I bought white corn meal from Costco and wanted to try making cornbread. In the past the other corn meals that I've used were very crummy. This recipe and this cornmeal are amazing! I like that it's dense and doesn't fall apart. I can eat for days. When it goes bad, I feed the rest to the birds, who love it as well!
I beat it for 5 minutes and it is wonderful!

Very tasty! Instead of the sugar I shook in pure stevia powder and also chopped up some green onions to mix into the batter. In place of the vegetable oil, I used a stick of butter. Served it with warm chili and the entire family was happy.
I do add a large spoon of sour cream to the batter.

I am confused how this turned out so bad. I didn't know it was possible to screw up cornbread. Putting it together you just knew this was different than any but hey I wanted new. This was just very weird texture. My husband called it chewy. The flavor was bland not fluffy at all. Wat too dense.
This is the ONLY recipe we use for our homemade cornbread, whether you're using it for a dinner with beans & ham, or like me using it to add to my homemade cornbread dressing, it's a keeper. !!
